recent_news.title: NEXTDC shares plunge 44% as power delays expose AI data centre bottleneck
recent_news.summary: NEXTDC’s downgrade is a stark example of a risk investors have tended to treat as theoretical: that grid access and local opposition, not customer demand, cap how fast data centre capacity can be built. The read-through extends well beyond Australia, as operators and AI cloud providers globally depend on utilities and planning authorities that move more slowly than hyperscaler spending plans. It echoes the warning in Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus, reported this week, that resistance to data centres is becoming more organised across jurisdictions. Investors may now apply a larger discount to contracted-but-undelivered capacity across the sector, particularly where projects depend on new grid connections.-NEXTDC had the customers and the contracts, but not the electricity, and its 44% share collapse shows the AI build-out now runs only as fast as the local grid and the local council allow.Summary:NEXTDC shares fell 44% in early trading after the company cut its FY27 guidanceUnderlying

recent_news.title: FX option expiries for 21 October 10am New York cut
recent_news.summary: There are a couple of key expiry levels to take note of on the day, as highlighted in bold below.The first ones are for EUR/USD with the expiries layered at the 1.1195 to 1.1200 region. The strikes are holding within 30 pips of the spot price and together, they are quite chunky in size. As such, the combined €4.3 billion in expiries could exert some pull towards the 1.1200 region heading into the cut. Or if anything else, they might also help reinforce the area as an intraday focal point.Having said that, broader euro and dollar sentiment will still take precedence alongside what else is happening with the bond market of course.The euro has its own set of problems with the France-Germany 10-year yield spread hitting 1.52% yesterday, its highest since 2012. That hasn't reverberated all too strongly yet but will continue to be a key risk factor for the single currency this week.Meanwhile, dollar sentiment is still very much tied to what is happening in the bond market. recent_news.title: NEXTDC shares plunge 44% as power delays expose AI data centre bottleneck
recent_news.summary: NEXTDC’s downgrade is a stark example of a risk investors have tended to treat as theoretical: that grid access and local opposition, not customer demand, cap how fast data centre capacity can be built. The read-through extends well beyond Australia, as operators and AI cloud providers globally depend on utilities and planning authorities that move more slowly than hyperscaler spending plans. It echoes the warning in Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus, reported this week, that resistance to data centres is becoming more organised across jurisdictions. Investors may now apply a larger discount to contracted-but-undelivered capacity across the sector, particularly where projects depend on new grid connections.-NEXTDC had the customers and the contracts, but not the electricity, and its 44% share collapse shows the AI build-out now runs only as fast as the local grid and the local council allow.Summary:NEXTDC shares fell 44% in early trading after the company cut its FY27 guidanceUnderlying

The strikes are holding within 30 pips of the spot price and together, they are quite chunky in size. As such, the combined €4.3 billion in expiries could exert some pull towards the 1.1200 region heading into the cut.
